title: Pharmacy First - Acute Otitis Media (AOM) Pathway (7a/7b/7c/7d)
description: Shared acute otitis media assessment with 4-route treatment selection: Otigo ear drops (symptomatic relief), amoxicillin, clarithromycin, erythromycin (pregnancy route 16-17 years).

fields.label: Signs/symptoms assessed and AOM diagnosis made using appropriate NICE CKS guidance
Otoscopy: moderate-severe bulging tympanic membrane with loss of landmarks and/or air-fluid level
Otoscopy: perforation of tympanic membrane and/or sticky discharge in external auditory canal
Known/suspected perforation of tympanic membrane (infectious/traumatic) including otorrhoea/myringotomy/grommet/ventilation tube
Under-2 with bilateral acute otitis media
Severe symptoms based on clinical global impression
Pain not adequately controlled with regular paracetamol/ibuprofen (age/weight appropriate dosing)
AOM symptom + otoscopy pattern met

History of severe immediate hypersensitivity to another beta-lactam (e.g. anaphylaxis)
Known hypersensitivity to any macrolide (clarithromycin/erythromycin) or route components

then.text: Urgent A&E referral required for sepsis or serious complications (e.g. meningitis, mastoiditis, intracranial abscess, sinus thrombosis, facial nerve paralysis).

validations.message: All AOM PGD routes require age 1 year and under 18 years.
Antibiotic AOM routes require under-2 bilateral with >3 days/severe symptoms OR AOM with otorrhoea.
Otigo 7a should not be used where the patient is in an antibiotic-benefit phenotype (under-2 bilateral AOM, or otorrhoea).
Otigo 7a requires moderate-severe symptoms and pain not adequately controlled with regular paracetamol/ibuprofen.
7d erythromycin is only for age 16-17, pregnant/suspected pregnancy, with amoxicillin/penicillin hypersensitivity (or severe immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity history).
7a Otigo quantity should be one appropriately labelled 15mL bottle.
7b amoxicillin quantity must match the selected age band.
Weight (kg) is required for clarithromycin dosing in children aged 1-11 years.

common_aom: Explain acute otitis media mainly affects children, can last around 1 week, and many children improve within 3 days without antibiotics.
Self-care: regular age/weight-appropriate paracetamol (and ibuprofen where appropriate).
Explain decongestants and antihistamines do not help symptoms.
Safety-net: seek medical advice if symptoms worsen rapidly/significantly, child becomes systemically very unwell, or not improving as expected.
otigo_7a: Instil 4 drops up to three times daily into affected ear(s).
Use until symptoms resolve or max 7 days.
Warm bottle in hands before each use.
Do not use if perforated eardrum/grommet/otorrhoea suspected (route exclusion logic already checked).
amoxicillin_7b: Explain exact dose and interval based on age band.
Can be taken with food or water.
Symptoms should start improving within 72 hours of taking amoxicillin; seek medical advice if no improvement/worse.
Advise urgent help for severe allergy/anaphylaxis symptoms.
clarithromycin_7c: Explain weight-based dosing (1-11 years) or fixed dose (12-17 years).
With or without food; suspension may cause bitter after-taste.
Counsel on interaction risks (e.g., statins, anticoagulants, QT-risk medicines) and when to seek urgent help.
Advise urgent help for severe allergy/anaphylaxis symptoms.
erythromycin_7d: Dose: 500mg four times daily (16-17 years pregnancy route).
Counsel on interaction/QT risk medicines and when to seek urgent help.
If breastfeeding applies, give infant monitoring advice (GI disturbance, oral candida, rash, drowsiness/irritability etc.).
Advise urgent help for severe allergy/anaphylaxis symptoms.

notes_for_implementation: AOM route split is clinically important: 7a is symptomatic pain relief only; 7b/7c/7d are antibiotic routes for specific AOM phenotypes.
Use otoscopic findings as explicit structured fields because multiple branch rules depend on perforation/otorrhoea status.
Keep a separate detailed medication interaction checker in production; checklist blockers here are a form-gating layer only.
Store route-family reasoning (why Otigo vs antibiotic) for audit and GP notification.
